$comment: Deploy targets. One entry per destination; `node scripts/deploy.mjs <target> <service>`
reads this. What each service IS lives in deploy/services.json.
Each target names THREE things that must agree, because they are three of the four ways
a deploy can land somewhere you did not mean:
account    the Zoho login the Catalyst CLI must be authenticated as. This is the one
setting that lives OUTSIDE the repo (machine-wide, see the guide §1.5), so
it is the only one a `cd` cannot get right for you. deploy.mjs reads the
CLI's own config and refuses to run when it does not match.
dc         Zoho data centre the account belongs to ('in', 'com', 'eu', ...). The CLI
keeps one login per DC, so the account check is meaningless without it.
catalystrc the .catalystrc payload — which Catalyst project + environment.
The fourth is per SERVICE, not per target, because two services in one project have
different secrets and different databases:
services.<name>.envFile     which git-ignored .env file supplies its env_variables.
services.<name>.appsail     optional. Overrides the default name in services.json,
so one service can be a different AppSail per account.
services.<name>.catalystrc  optional. Overrides the target's, for a service that
lives in its own Catalyst project rather than beside
the others.
Adding a target: add an entry with an envFile for every service, add its
deploy/<name>.catalystrc.json, and create the env files from the matching examples.
Nothing else needs to change.
